title: Constantinople VIII (869): Christ’s image to be honored like the Gospels—refuse adoration and miss His face at the Second Coming
source_text: XIII. Doctrinam istius Synodi confirmat Concilium quod octavum Generale dicitur, celebratum, ut diximus, in urbe Constantinopoli, anno Christi 869. Nam Actione decima hic est tertius ejus Canon. Sacram Domini Nostri Jesu Christi effigiem, eadem qua sancta Evangelia veneratione colendam statuimus. Quemadmodum enim per syllabas ex Evangelio pronunciatas salutem consequuntur omnes, ita per imagines arte coloribusque pictas & expressas, docti juxta & indocti ex objecta re utilitatem capiunt. Quaecunque enim in syllabis oratio, hoc in coloribus pictura docet & repraesentat. Ergo quicunque Christi salvatoris imaginem non adorat, is in secundo Christi adventu non videat ipsius faciem. Eadem ratione intemeratae genitricis ejus effigiem, Sanctorumque Angelorum, quemadmodum illos sacrarum literarum paginae describunt, ac divorum omnium veneramur & adoramus. Qui aliter sentiunt Anathema sunto. Quod autem Concilium istud imagines, ratione cultus & venerationis, cum Evangelio comparat, respicit morem Graecorum, qui ipsum codicem Evangeliorum certis ritibus colunt & adorant, ut fit de imagine Crucis.
pass_a_gloss: The doctrine of that Synod is confirmed by the Council which is called the eighth General, celebrated, as we said, in the city of Constantinople in the year of Christ 869. For in the tenth Action this is its third Canon. We decree that the sacred effigy of Our Lord Jesus Christ is to be cultivated with the same veneration as the holy Gospels. For just as through syllables pronounced from the Gospel all obtain salvation, so through images painted and expressed by art and colors the learned and the unlearned alike take utility from the object set before them. For whatever speech teaches in syllables, this painting teaches and represents in colors. Therefore whoever does not adore the image of Christ the Savior, let him not see His face at Christ’s second coming. By the same reason we venerate and adore the effigy of His undefiled mother, and of the Holy Angels as the pages of sacred letters describe them, and of all the saints. Let those who think otherwise be Anathema. But that this Council compares images, as to cult and veneration, with the Gospel, looks to the custom of the Greeks, who cultivate and adore the very codex of the Gospels with certain rites, as is done concerning the image of the Cross.
pass_b_english: The ‘eighth’ Council ranks Christ’s image with Gospel-veneration: paint teaches as syllables teach.
Refuse to adore Christ’s image, and you are cursed not to see His face at His return.
Greek Gospel-book rites explain the parallel.
